checks.value: The information found on our website is not part of this or any other report we file with
Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties
Changes in weather where we operate may increase the costs of powering and cooling computer hardware
The following Management’s Discussion and Analysis

provenance: Same fixture/filing as msft-2013-structure.json (see its provenance for the whitespace-collapse-first normalization method needed for this filing and the ALL-CAPS body-heading pattern). CANON FIX (per specs/decisions/ADR-003-stdlib-normalization.md's 'Normalization canon' section, added in the T2 dual-pass audit): item 7's opening-sentence anchor was originally written as ASCII "The following Management's Discussion and Analysis" against a scratch renderer that had silently transliterated the fixture's curly apostrophe ('’') to a straight ASCII quote -- dead under ADR-003's canon (entities decode to real Unicode and stay Unicode, no transliteration). Re-verified 2026-08-15 with `python3 -c` using `html.unescape` (not grep on raw bytes) against a canon-correct rendering: raw whitespace (including literal source newlines, see the structure case's provenance) collapsed to single spaces FIRST, block tags converted to newlines, tags stripped, entities unescaped, THEN a second whitespace collapse pass (catching ` ` -> U+00A0, which only becomes whitespace-shaped AFTER unescaping, so a single pre-unescape collapse alone silently misses it -- this second-pass gap was caught and fixed while re-verifying this case, not present in the original authoring pass). Item spans bounded by consecutive ALL-CAPS heading positions in the canon-correct rendering: item 1 [6315,50196), item 1A [50196,89121), item 7 [94697,179368), item 8 [183083,293756) (0-indexed chars) -- lengths shift by a handful of chars from the original measurements (NBSP-collapse differences), all well inside the existing bands, no band changes needed. Occurrence counts (global document, case-sensitive exact string, canon rendering): 'Microsoft was founded in 1975' = 1 (item 1's true opening sentence, right after the ALL-CAPS heading and a 'GENERAL' sub-heading); 'The information found on our website is not part of this or any other report we file with' = 1, item 1's true last sentence before page furniture ('13 / Table of Contents / PART I / Item 1A') and the Item 1A heading follow -- picked deliberately over the raw tail text specifically to avoid anchoring on furniture. 'Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties' = 1, item 1A's opening sentence. 'Changes in weather where we operate may increase the costs of powering and cooling computer hardware' = 1, item 1A's true last sentence before Item 1B begins. 'The following Management’s Discussion and Analysis' (CANON-FIXED: curly apostrophe U+2019, was a dead ASCII "'" anchor, count=0 under canon before the fix) = 1, item 7's opening sentence. 'Frank H. Brod' = 3 total: the first (inside item 7's span, at the very end -- a Chief-Accounting-Officer sign-off paragraph that is item 7's genuine last content) is the one this check targets; the other two are in the formal SIGNATURES page at the very end of the whole document (outside any item), so they do not threaten this check's discriminating power for item 7 specifically. 'INCOME STATEMENTS' = 2, both inside item 8 (the literal 'INCOME STATEMENTS' sub-heading right after the Item 8 heading, and 'COMPREHENSIVE INCOME STATEMENTS' a few paragraphs later, which contains it as a substring) -- both legitimately inside the item, so still a valid presence check. 'Seattle, Washington' = 4 total: 1 inside Item 1A (a Properties/Legal-Proceedings-adjacent mention of MSFT's Seattle headquarters area, well before Item 1A's end), 2 inside Item 8 (Deloitte's two audit-opinion sign-offs -- financial statements opinion and ICFR opinion -- the second of which, at the very end of Item 8's span, is the true last-paragraph anchor), 1 further out inside Item 9A (a third, later Deloitte opinion reference, outside Item 8). Kept as an existence anchor for item 8 despite the outside-item hits, same reasoning as AAPL's 'macroeconomic': the check only inspects text inside whatever span the extractor labels item 8, so hits elsewhere in the document do not make the check pass falsely -- they would only matter if the extractor's boundary badly bled forward past item 9's start into item 9A, which no other check in this case would catch either, so it is a known, accepted limit of text_contains-style checks, not unique to this anchor. REJECTED as an anchor: 'DELOITTE & TOUCHE LLP\nSeattle, Washington\nJuly 30, 2013' as a single combined phrase -- these three pieces sit in separate block elements in the raw HTML, so a paragraph-preserving normalizer inserts real newlines between them (same class of risk as AAPL's rejected 'San Jose, California October 31, 2025' combined anchor); using 'Seattle, Washington' alone avoids the ambiguity. text_not_contains checks guard against the item bleeding forward into the next item's heading text (RISK FACTORS / UNRESOLVED STAFF COMMENTS / QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE / CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS, all in the ALL-CAPS form used by this filing's real headings) -- re-verified 0 occurrences inside each item's own span under the canon rendering. min_chars/max_chars bands derived from the original measured raw span lengths (unchanged, the new canon lengths are within a few dozen chars of these and still comfortably inside band): item 1 = 43956 chars (band 30000-65000), item 1A = 39035 chars (band 25000-58000), item 7 = 84741 chars (band 60000-125000), item 8 = 110762 chars (band 80000-160000) -- roughly 65-70% of measured for the floor and 140-150% for the ceiling, generous enough to tolerate a different real normalizer's exact character count while still catching a badly truncated or badly bloated (cross-item-bleed) extraction. stats (measured char length / rough paragraph count via non-blank newline-delimited segments / digit-density = digit chars over total chars, same rendering, approximate and normalizer-implementation-dependent, not re-measured on the canon-corrected text this pass since the length deltas are negligible): item 1 -- len=43956, paragraphs~=186, digit_density=0.011; item 1A -- len=39035, paragraphs~=95, digit_density=0.004; item 7 -- len=84741, paragraphs~=565, digit_density=0.037; item 8 -- len=110762, paragraphs~=1695 (heavily table-driven -- financial-statement rows/cells each become a line in this rendering, so this over-counts true prose paragraphs by a wide margin, flagged as a proxy not a literal claim), digit_density=0.070 (order of magnitude above the prose items, as expected for financial tables). Not independently re-verified by extraction-auditor as of this authoring pass -- flagged for dual-pass (this is a rewrite, will be re-audited).
